      Transfer block

      The block contains your keys, protected by the code. Never send block and code the same way (for example, not both in one e-mail). Each click makes a new code.

      Emergency sheet

      A page with everything needed to open the vault — even without CryptBridge. Print it and keep it like a house key. It is not saved anywhere by CryptBridge.

      Drive

      Drive letter and cache can only be changed while the drive is disconnected. Files that are still waiting for upload stay in the old cache folder — finish uploads before you move it.

      Behaviour

      App lock — recommended

      With an app password, CryptBridge starts locked and locks itself again when you lock Windows (Win+L) or sign out. Locked, the drive is closed (after running uploads are done), rclone is stopped, and the cache with readable copies of your files is deleted. The pCloud sign-in and the vault keys are stored sealed with the app password. The emergency sheet and the transfer block ask for it, too.

      The app password is not the vault password: if you forget it, your files are not lost — you set CryptBridge up again with the emergency sheet.

      State

      Own pCloud app — recommended

      CryptBridge signs in to pCloud through rclone. Without an own app it uses rclone's shared access, which pCloud has blocked for hours at a time before (most recently on 5 October 2026). With your own app, CryptBridge no longer depends on it. Your vault stays exactly as it is — same keys, same files; you only sign in once more.

      In use now
      rclone's shared access
      How to get your own pCloud app (once; pCloud has to approve it)
      1. Open , log in with your pCloud account and request a new application.
      2. Fill in the request exactly like this, then click Create request:
        App nameCryptBridge (personal)
        Application TypePersonal use
        Folder accessAll folders — your vault is a normal folder in your pCloud
        Write accessYes — needed to upload files
        Websitehttps://github.com/burnersen/CryptBridge
        Expected number of users1
        ReasonPersonal use only. I use the open-source tool CryptBridge (https://github.com/burnersen/CryptBridge), which is based on rclone, to access my own pCloud account: it shows an encrypted folder of my pCloud as a drive on my own computers. Only my own pCloud account will use this app. It needs access to all folders because my existing encrypted folders are not inside an app folder, and write access to upload my files.
      3. Wait until pCloud approves the app. This can take a while — so request it now, before you need it.
      4. Open the approved app on My Apps and add this address under Redirect URIs:
        Without it, pCloud answers the sign-in with “redirect_uri is not authorized”.
      5. Copy the app's Client ID and Client secret into the fields below and click Save app, then sign in again when CryptBridge asks.
      6. Linux server (not urgent — its sign-in keeps working until pCloud blocks rclone's shared access again): create a new transfer block on the Vault tab, run sudo cryptbridge setup on the server, answer n to “Keep the pCloud sign-in and vault keys from the last setup?” and paste the block.

      The codes are stored encrypted with your Windows account, like your pCloud sign-in. They are not part of the transfer block: the server needs only the sign-in itself.
